Although the CDC is reporting only 27 illnesses in a Salmonella Telelkebir outbreak linked to oysters, the Virginia Department of Health has documented 55 patients across 19 states.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention report on Oct. 19 counted patients in 12 states. The Food and Drug Administration reported the same number in a recall notice for oysters harvested by the Little Wicomico Oyster Company from the Little Wicomico River.

The Virginia health department reports that the illnesses began in late May and run through Oct. 6. The CDC reports that five patients have required hospitalization. Georgia’s Department of Agriculture says Publix sold the recalled oysters as “James River Oysters” through Oct. 14, five days after the recall.

For the 27 patients reported by the CDC, 10 reported eating raw oysters. Tag and traceback records exist for seven. Two of the seven ate oysters from a single Virginia source and five from several, and the company’s Little Wicomico River oysters were the only oysters in common to the seven ill people included in traceback.

title: Mixed response to EU frozen meat plans
summary:
There has been a mixed reaction to planned regulation changes in Europe that would give companies more flexibility on when they can freeze meat.

The proposals would increase the options for businesses around storage conditions before freezing meat. They are based on a European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) opinion.
